exposed_env.name: Leaked secrets and files
exposed_env.description: Looks for files that should never be public, like .env files, a .git folder or cloud keys, that can hand attackers your passwords and API keys.

security_headers.name: Browser security headers
security_headers.description: Checks the protective headers (CSP, HSTS and others) and cookie settings that tell browsers how to keep your visitors safe.

tls_cert.name: HTTPS and certificate
tls_cert.description: Makes sure your site uses HTTPS, redirects to it, and has a valid certificate that isn't about to expire.

open_admin.name: Exposed admin and debug pages
open_admin.description: Finds admin panels, database tools and debug consoles that are reachable by anyone on the internet.

default_creds.name: Unfinished installers
default_creds.description: Spots setup wizards and installers that were left open, which could let a stranger take over your app.

info_leak.name: Information leaks
info_leak.description: Notices when your site reveals software versions, error details, debug mode or folder listings that help attackers plan.

landing.title: Know what's exposed on your site, in plain language.
landing.subtitle: Enter your site's address and GuardHub checks the gaps attackers actually use: leaked secrets, open admin pages, weak HTTPS. You get clear answers and step-by-step fixes, not jargon.
landing.ctaNote: No sign-up needed. You'll only need to prove the site is yours.

enter.title: Enter
enter.body: Type your website's address and prove it's yours with a small file, a meta tag or a DNS record. It takes about two minutes.

see.title: See
see.body: Watch each check run live. Your report shows what's exposed and why it matters, with no stack traces and no jargon.

fix.title: Fix
fix.body: Every finding comes with clear, step-by-step fix instructions. Rescan any time to confirm the gap is closed.

checks.title: What we check
checks.intro: Six focused checks that cover the problems behind most real-world break-ins of small web apps.

promise.title: Do no harm, with your permission
promise.intro: A security tool has to be trustworthy first. These rules are built into GuardHub, not just written down.

permission.title: Permission first
permission.body: We only scan a website after you've proved you control it. Nobody can use GuardHub to probe someone else's site.

passive.title: Passive and gentle
passive.body: Our checks only read what's already public. We never change data, try passwords or put load on your servers, and we keep every scan rate-limited.

privacy.title: Your data stays private
privacy.body: Anything sensitive we find is masked before it's stored, so even the evidence never shows a full secret. We keep only what your report needs. To find the subdomains of your verified domain, GuardHub searches the public Certificate Transparency logs (crt.sh): your domain name, which is already public in those logs, is sent to that service, and no other data is shared. If you connect GitHub repositories, their dependencies and contents are read to find vulnerable packages and secrets committed to the code; your code is not stored. To look up known vulnerabilities, only package names and versions are sent to OSV (api.osv.dev).

final.title: Find out where you stand in a few minutes
final.body: Your first scan is free and doesn't need an account.

trustedDomains.adminCardBody: Prove once that you control a site, then scan exactly that address without the proof prompt.
trustedDomains.intro: Add a site you control and prove it once with one of the usual methods. After that you can scan it from here without being asked for the proof again.
trustedDomains.ruleOnce: You prove ownership once, with a verification file, a meta tag or a DNS TXT record.
trustedDomains.ruleKeep: Keep the proof published. We check it again every day. If it's gone, the domain is suspended and scans stop until you verify it again.
trustedDomains.ruleExact: Only the exact address is covered: the same host, port and http/https. Subdomains such as www or app need their own entry.
trustedDomains.ruleOthers: Every other site still needs the normal ownership proof. Only you can see your trusted domains.

modules.title: Module Center
modules.intro: Every check and feature, its lab accuracy, how it behaves in production, and its switches.
modules.ruleBody: A check can only be switched on when the validation lab measured it in CI and it met the gate (at least 95% precision and 80% recall). Active tests (beta) also stay off until the founder's checkpoint. Locked modules show the reason instead of a switch. Switching off is always allowed.

reports.title: Reports
reports.intro: Platform, module, scan, finding and customer reports and the risk trend. Customer data is always masked, on screen and in every export. Exports are recorded in the audit log.

kindHelp.platform: One row per day: scans by outcome, new findings by severity, new accounts.
kindHelp.modules: One row per check: runs, could not run, findings by severity, false positives.
kindHelp.scans: Every scan in the period (up to 5,000), sites masked.
kindHelp.findings: Findings per check and severity, with the admin's triage.
kindHelp.customers: One row per customer account (masked): projects, scans and serious findings.
kindHelp.risk_trend: One row per week: completed scans, their average score, critical and high findings.

reports.truncated: the export holds every row up to the limit
reports.schedulesIntro: A platform summary e-mailed to every admin: counts and a link only, never rows.

integrations.title: API & integrations
integrations.intro: Keys for integrations such as a CI pipeline, and the traffic of every API endpoint.
integrations.boundaryTitle: What a key can never do

boundary.noAdmin: A key never opens a session: the admin console and its API refuse it.
boundary.userRole: A key acts as its owner in the customer role, so it sees the owner's own projects and scans only, even when the owner is an admin.
boundary.proof: A scan started with a key still needs a fresh ownership proof (§9.2). Active tests can never be started with a key.
boundary.hashed: Only a hash of the key is stored. The key is shown once, when it is created.
boundary.limits: Every key expires (at most 365 days), can be revoked at any time and is limited to 120 requests a minute. Creation, revocation and every scan it starts are audited.
boundary.webhooks: Webhooks go only to public https:// addresses on port 443: every address the name resolves to is checked, the request goes to the checked address and redirects are never followed. Scan events go only to the scan owner's webhooks.

integrations.howTo: Send the key as a bearer token. Requests that change something also need the X-GuardHub-CSRF header.
integrations.keysIntro: A key belongs to the admin who creates it.
integrations.secretOnce: Key “{name}” created. Copy it now: it will not be shown again.
integrations.secretWarning: Store it in your integration's secret store. If it is lost, revoke it and create a new one.
integrations.trafficIntro: Per route, from every API process. Routes are shown as templates, never with identifiers.
integrations.noTraffic: No traffic recorded in this period.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.intro: Signed HTTPS calls when something happens. Every request carries an X-GuardHub-Signature header.
webhooks.name: Name
webhooks.urlHelp: https:// only, port 443, a public host name.
webhooks.secretOnce: Webhook “{name}” added. Copy its signing secret now: it will not be shown again.
webhooks.secretHelp: Use it to verify the X-GuardHub-Signature header on every request.
webhooks.verifyHelp: Verify a request: HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>" with the signing secret must equal v1, and t must be recent (5 minutes). Failed deliveries are retried up to 3 times for network errors, 429 and 5xx.

people.title: Users & sessions
people.intro: Accounts, sessions, admin invitations and failed sign-ins. Customers and admins only: there is no role matrix.

policy.mfa: Two-factor sign-in is required for every account before it can use GuardHub.
policy.adminMfa: The admin console needs a two-factor session and an admin role read from the database on every request.
policy.disabled: A disabled account cannot sign in. Its sessions end at once, its API keys stop and its scheduled scans wait.
policy.invites: An admin invitation works once, for 72 hours, only for the invited e-mail after two-factor sign-in.
policy.rbac: Roles are customer and admin. Data boundaries are enforced by the database (row-level security). A full role matrix is not part of this release.

people.invitesIntro: Send the link through a channel you trust. It is shown once.
people.linkOnce: Invitation created. Copy the link now: it will not be shown again.
people.linkHelp: The person signs in (or signs up) with exactly this e-mail, completes two-factor sign-in, then opens the link.
people.failedIntro: Wrong passwords and wrong two-factor codes. Addresses are shown as a keyed hash.
people.failedTotal: {count, plural, one {# failed sign-in} other {# failed sign-ins}}
people.noFailed: No failed sign-ins in the last 24 hours.
people.inviteEmailed: The invitation was e-mailed to the address. The link is also shown here once.
people.inviteNotEmailed: E-mail is not configured: send the link yourself through a trusted channel.
people.resetHelp: Ends every session of this account and deletes its recovery codes. It must sign in with its password and set up two-factor again.
